names_for.catalogue_side: Data APIs (consumption-based: Street Level Imagery, AI Event Videos, Road Detections)
names_for.custom_side: Burst (on-demand mapping); also Bee Edge AI for custom workloads on network devices

operator_role.note: Bee Maps sells its own data under its own name; its ToS makes it owner of data collected from Bees. No separate buyer licence document was found.

economics_model.note: Bee Maps owns the data and sells at its own list prices; contributor rewards are funded by Bee Maps at its discretion, not a share of each sale.

who_pays_fee.note: No marketplace fee: Bee Maps is the only seller and sells its own data at list price.

supply_models.note: Crowd drivers and fleets running Bee dashcams. Beekeeper fleet customers' data is also owned by Bee Maps (sale limited to aggregated or anonymized data). Whether Burst captures ordered by one buyer are resold to others is not stated.

custody_model.note: Platform-hosted; buyers receive temporary signed URLs and download the files.

transaction_mode.note: Self-serve prepaid API balance for all data APIs; a contact form for training-data and other needs.

public_prices.note: Every data API and Burst has a published unit price; no price is published for whatever is agreed through the contact form.

licence_model.note: Only marketing statements (AI Event Videos licensed for commercial use incl. training; 'flexible licensing') were found; no buyer licence or data terms document.

exclusivity_offered.note: Nothing found either way for buyers.

public_listing.note: Products and prices are public; querying imagery, clips or detections needs an API key from an account.

buyer_vetting.note: An account and API key; no credit card needed to start with free credits. No business verification found.

sample_mechanics.note: No separate sample set; new accounts get USD 20 in free credits usable on real data before paying.

versioning.note: Imagery is time-indexed (per week or latest) rather than versioned; no statement on versions or withdrawals.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Approach is automatic blurring of faces, bodies, vehicles and plates before upload plus removal requests; no buyer licence found to say whether any consent warranty or evidence is given.

contributor_pay_model.note: Network terms pay Map Coverage Rewards for collecting and Consumption Rewards when paid demand is fulfilled; Burst adds targeted incentives; from August 2026 rewards are in USDC funded by Bee Maps at its discretion. Rates not published.

erasure_after_sale.note: Removal and blurring requests exist, but nothing says whether copies already downloaded by buyers must be deleted.

quality_evidence.note: Bee Maps is operator and sole provider, so the operator/provider distinction does not fit; no quality statement on listings was found beyond vendor claims about freshness.

Q1.answer: Bee Maps sells per image (USD 0.005) and per event clip (USD 6) and names world-model and AV training as uses; it says enterprise customers include HERE, Lyft, NBC Universal, Mapbox and Volkswagen (vendor-stated). Volumes bought are not published.

Q3.answer: Inventory comes from crowd drivers and fleets running Bee dashcams; Bee Maps' ToS says it owns data collected from Bees and from Beekeeper fleets, while the May 2026 Hivemapper network terms say contributors keep ownership and license each developer whose Work Order is fulfilled.

Q4.answer: Burst lets one buyer pay to have drivers capture an area, but nothing says whether that imagery is then sold to others. Terms moved: ToS updated Q4 2025, network terms May 2026, and HONEY rewards replaced by Bee-Maps-funded USDC from August 2026.

Q5.answer: Bee Maps sells as owner and licensor of the data under its own name; no buyer licence was found, so who warrants consent and who indemnifies the buyer is unknown.

Q6.answer: Platform-hosted; buyers query the API and receive temporary signed URLs to download images and clips into their own systems.

Q7.answer: Capturers: covered by Bee Maps ToS ownership and the network licence to developers; Beekeeper data is not anonymized as to drivers. Depicted people and property: automatic on-device blurring plus blur/delete on request; no release evidence found.

Q8.answer: Bee Maps says AI Event Videos are licensed for commercial use including training and derivatives, and imagery allows derived datasets; exclusivity, audit, leakage controls and fingerprinting are not addressed in anything found.

Q9.answer: Self-serve: a prepaid USD API balance, debited per call at list price, with no subscription or minimum; a contact form handles training-data and other requests. Bee Maps owns the inventory, so there is no commission.

Q10.answer: The unit sold is an image, an event clip, a batch of detections or a Burst location, each debited per API call; imagery is indexed by week or latest, and a history endpoint logs credit use. Nothing on versions or withdrawals.

Q11.answer: Before paying, a buyer gets USD 20 of free credits on an account with no card; trust signals are vendor claims of coverage and freshness, not independent evidence.

Q12.answer: The catalogue side is the consumption-priced 'Data APIs'; the bespoke side is 'Burst (on-demand mapping)', which pushes paid capture requests to nearby drivers through the same API and balance, plus Bee Edge AI for custom workloads on network devices.

unknowns.note: No data-buyer licence or API data terms found; the ToS index lists only Bee and Bee Membership terms. A prior document profile noted a 'Data Products' tab on /tos that is not in served text.
What the buyer receives about consent is unknown without buyer terms.
Whether Bee Maps also lists on third-party marketplaces (cloud exchanges etc.) could not be checked without web search.
Whether imagery captured for one buyer's Burst joins the general catalogue sold to others is not stated.
No USDC or HONEY rates per km, per Burst or per consumption event were published on pages fetched.
EDGAR full-text search returned no Form D for Hivemapper; customer names, km and coverage figures are vendor-stated only. Independent press could not be discovered without web search.

conflicts.resolution: Bee Maps ToS (Q4 2025) says Bee Maps owns data it collects from a Bee; the Hivemapper network terms (May 2026) say Hivemapper claims no rights in Contributor Data and contributors license developers. Both may hold if Bee Maps acts as a 'developer' on the network, but the documents do not reconcile this; both kept.
Network terms dated May 2026 still describe HONEY rewards; the July 2026 announcement ends HONEY support from August 2026. Newer event wins for the current reward currency.
